title: Pistachios vs. almonds: nutrition differences

seo.title: Pistachios vs. almonds: nutrition comparison
seo.meta_description: Per 30 g, pistachios and almonds provide roughly 168–175 calories and about 6 g protein. Almonds lead in fiber and magnesium; pistachios in potassium.
seo.search_intent: Compare pistachios and almonds for calories, protein, fiber and minerals

excerpt: Pistachios and almonds are close in calories and protein: per 30 g, raw pistachios provide about 168 calories and 6.2 g protein, while raw almonds provide about 175 calories and 6.5 g. In current USDA Foundation references, almonds provide more fiber and magnesium; pistachios provide more potassium. There is no overall nutritional winner.
content_html:
It is easy to try to crown a winner between pistachios and almonds based on a fraction of a gram of protein. In a normal serving, calories and protein are almost a tie; fiber and several minerals are more informative differences.

Compare 30 g of each, raw

Per 30 gPistachiosAlmonds
Calories~168~175
Protein~6.2 g~6.5 g
Fat~13.5 g~15.3 g
Fiber~2.1 g~3.2 g
Magnesium~33 mg~77 mg
Potassium~284 mg~220 mg
Calcium~35 mg~76 mg

The values come from current USDA Foundation references; cultivar and roasting can shift composition.

Protein: a practical tie

Pistachios provide about 20.5 g protein/100 g and almonds 21.5 g. At 30 g, the gap is only around 0.3 g—too small to make protein a compelling reason to choose one.

Almonds: more fiber and magnesium

The current almond reference contains 10.8 g fiber and 258 mg magnesium/100 g. The pistachio reference contains about 7.0 g and 110 mg. The magnesium difference is substantial even after scaling to a handful.

Pistachios: more potassium here

Pistachios provide about 947 mg potassium/100 g versus 733 mg in almonds. At 30 g, that is roughly 284 versus 220 mg.

Shell weight is not edible weight

With in-shell pistachios, purchased weight includes material you do not eat. Nutrition databases compare the edible kernels. The shells may still affect eating behavior by slowing the pace and making the amount consumed more visible.

Which should you choose?

Almonds if fiber, magnesium or calcium is the priority; pistachios if you prefer their potassium profile, flavor or in-shell format. For calories and protein, the differences are too small to support a universal hierarchy.

faq.question: Which has more protein, pistachios or almonds?
faq.answer: They are very close: about 20.5 versus 21.5 g/100 g.

faq.question: Which has more fiber?
faq.answer: Almonds in the current Foundation references: about 10.8 versus 7.0 g/100 g.

faq.question: Which has more potassium?
faq.answer: Pistachios in this comparison: about 947 versus 733 mg/100 g.
